I suppose psu sensor would also has an Unavailable interface, if yes, then it should be marked as true while the sensor reading is being skipped.
Done
I question if this should be pushed from the update process vs the monitor knowing that firmware update update flow.

You mean something like a DBus method or property to pause the reading from fw update side? Or is there already something which can be used.

Are there any tradeoffs which make it better to perform the logic on fw update side.

Some net comments here:
The intent of specifying the type in the EM config is so that we can make decisions like this based on the actual behavior of the device.  I don't see that handled, and presumably you didn't check all 100+ devices datasheets to verify that they can't handle sensor polling at the same time as update, so I would expect some amount of lookup table there.

The other intent of reactors was that one application would handle communication to the device, to make things like this easy to manage.  As written, there's still races around if a sensor read is in progress when an update starts, and I don't know how to handle that without a complex IPC, or one application managing the device.

@paligill@gmail.com I think i mentioned this use case on your design.  Was this covered there?

> As written, there's still races around if a sensor read is in progress when an update starts, and I don't know how to handle that without a complex IPC, or one application managing the device.
> 
> @paligill@gmail.com I think i mentioned this use case on your design.  Was this covered there?

Sorry, i don't remember if any such case was mentioned during design discussions. For the other point you mentioned about the race condition, i can understand it can happen, probably may need some hold down time before starting an upgrade to let the channel clear up.

Yes, Software.I2CVR needs to wait a while after changing Activation and before starting the upgrade.

Not all VR devices require monitoring to be paused during firmware updates.
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/83964
uses `FirmwareName` as an opt-in mechanism. Add it to the EM config only for VR devices that experience PMBus conflicts during updates. Devices without this property continue monitoring uninterrupted.

> uses FirmwareName as an opt-in mechanism. Add it to the EM config only for VR devices that experience PMBus conflicts during updates

The "Firmware name" doesn't determine whether a device handles updates or not.  That's not a per-system decision, that's a per-device decision, so it goes in code, not an EM config.

Original issue is still present, I'm not sure why this was resolved.

Changed to use a lookup table of specific firmware types. psusensor scans EM config for these firmware types and builds a mapping by bus/address. Only sensors whose bus/address matches these firmware configs get paused during updates. It reuses existing I2CVR firmware configurations without requiring new EM properties.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/+/85233
adds a delay after changing Activation and before starting the upgrade, giving psusensor time to detect the signal and pause polling before firmware commands begin.
DOesn't look resolved.  The root here looks like someone bypassed the "type should represent the hardware" and split the config into two.  That needs fixed before this can go.
Lets name firmwareAssociations to something better as it gets confused with Dbus association, but looks like this a local object to store the state.
OK. changed to firmwareUpdateStates.
Shouldn't you skip if the activating state was unchanged?
Done. Thanks for the suggestion.
Can you please add a comment about why are you creating this name for lookup and which object state are you trying to update?
combineEvents is the existing map of PSUEvent instances. PSUEvent instances poll sysfs attributes such as xxx_crit_alarm and xxx_lcrit_alarm.
Can you split this function into two? One setting up the match, the other handling the firmware update, both called from main?
separated to `setupFirmwareUpdateMatch()` setting up the match for Activation signal; `checkInitialFwUpdateState` checking initial firmware component Activation state.
These paths aren't connected at all.  There's no gaurantee that these names are the same device in the em config.
This means everything is going to spin while the update is happening.  We should jsut stop/start the timer when we get stop/start events.
Done
I'm fairly certain this isn't an interface we define.
xyz.openbmc_project.Software.I2CVR is the bus name of the i2c-vr update daemon.
Lets get this code cleaned up a little.  we have "one" line of code that's stretched across 20 lines and includes a ton of lambdas and properties.
Done

Overall this looks like someone modeled a device incorrectly in EM config and is now trying to make up for it in a bunch of code.  Add the device to a top level exposes type, and add whatever properties are needed on the backend to update it.  From there PSUsensor can coordinate with the firmware update however we want it to.
Please don't use regex in new code.  std::regex is famously slow.
Done
?  What is this even doing?
It strips the trailing number. e.g., converting `Yosemite5_MB_VR_CPU0_MEM_3602` to `Yosemite5_MB_VR_CPU0_MEM`
Why are we doing another hunt for firmware types and trying to do a matchup?  We know all the details from the exposes record.  If we need to add more details, add them.
